chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem with coitus interruptus (al-'azl) from the free woman if her husband likes it, and if she dislikes it, she has no authority in the matter.

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ الْحُرَّةِ: The free woman (as opposed to a slave)
key_terms.مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْ‏ءٌ: Authority or right in the matter

ai.seo_question: Is a wife's consent required for coitus interruptus in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that coitus interruptus (al-'azl) is legally permissible (mubah) for a free wife, emphasizing that the husband's unilateral decision suffices regardless of her consent. In Shia jurisprudence, this reflects the principle of the husband's authority over marital intimacy, though later scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Tusi noted that while not invalidating the act, it is recommended to seek her agreement to avoid discord. The ruling specifically applies to free women, distinguishing it from concubinage where the master's will is absolute.
